name: Pi
tagline: An extensible coding agent and toolkit for terminal interfaces and language-model integrations.
hook: A shared-checkout guide to session safety, coordination, model catalogs, isolated tests, interactive checks, and releases.
summary: Pi protects multiple agent sessions working in one checkout and asks them to communicate briefly. It names the source files behind generated code, separates safe tests from live-provider calls, and sends interactive testing and releases to focused guides.

techniques.title: Protect other sessions through explicit Git boundaries
techniques.body: The Git section explains why broad staging, resets, cleaning, and stashing can interfere with other sessions. It requires explicit file paths and checking staged ownership before committing.
techniques.quote:
Committing:

- Only commit files YOU changed in THIS session.
- Stage explicit paths (`git add <path1> <path2>`); never `git add -A` / `git add .`.
- Before committing, run `git status` and verify you are only staging your files.
- `packages/ai/src/models.generated.ts` may always be included alongside your files.
- Message format: `{feat,fix,docs}[(ai,tui,agent,coding-agent)]: <commit message> (optionally multiple lines)`. Message is informative and concise.

Never run (destroys other agents' work or bypasses checks):

- `git reset --hard`, `git checkout .`, `git clean -fd`, `git stash`, `git add -A`, `git add .`, `git commit --no-verify`.

techniques.title: Name the generator and permit its legitimate output
techniques.body: The model catalog may not be edited directly. Its generator is the authority, and the rule explicitly permits generated metadata updates that accompany regeneration.
techniques.quote: - Never modify `packages/ai/src/models.generated.ts` directly; update `packages/ai/scripts/generate-models.ts` instead, then regenerate. Including the resulting `models.generated.ts` diff is always OK, even if regeneration includes unrelated upstream model metadata changes.

techniques.title: Keep regression tests away from real providers
techniques.body: The coding-agent suite uses its harness and a faux provider. The rule explicitly excludes real API credentials and paid tokens from that test path.
techniques.quote: - For `packages/coding-agent/test/suite/`, use `test/suite/harness.ts` + the faux provider. No real provider APIs, keys, or paid tokens.

techniques.title: Separate dependency installation from lifecycle execution
techniques.body: Dependency changes are reviewed as code, and install commands disable lifecycle scripts. New dependencies with lifecycle scripts need review and an explicit allowlist entry in the shrinkwrap generator.
techniques.quote:
- Hydrate/update locally with `npm install --ignore-scripts`; clean/CI-style with `npm ci --ignore-scripts`. Don't run lifecycle scripts unless the user asks.
- If dep metadata changes, refresh `package-lock.json` with `npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts`.
- If `packages/coding-agent/npm-shrinkwrap.json` needs regen, run `node scripts/generate-coding-agent-shrinkwrap.mjs` (verify with `--check` or `npm run check`). New deps with lifecycle scripts require review and an explicit allowlist entry in that script; never add one silently.

techniques.title: Use task guides for interactive testing and releases
techniques.body: The root rules link to separate guides for exercising the interactive agent and preparing or recovering releases. Those procedures are loaded when that work is requested.
techniques.quote: For testing pi's interactive mode, load and follow [.pi/skills/interactive-testing.md](.pi/skills/interactive-testing.md).

steal: Limit shared-checkout Git operations to explicitly owned paths.
Pair generated-file prohibitions with the generator and allowed output changes.
Use a fake provider for tests that should never consume live API tokens.
Review dependency lifecycle scripts separately from dependency installation.
outline: Testing pi Interactive Mode with tmux
